name: Eclipse
identity_check: Confirmed as Eclipse (eclipse.capital; the old domain eclipse.vc 301-redirects there), the Palo Alto VC that Lior Susan started in 2015 (TechCrunch 2019, 2026) and that invests in the physical economy. Office 514 High Street, Palo Alto; the site's company LinkedIn page is linkedin.com/company/eclipse-vc. The firm now calls itself just 'Eclipse' (site, fund posts, ©2026 Eclipse); press still writes 'Eclipse Ventures' (TechCrunch, VCJ/PEI, SiliconANGLE) and sometimes 'Eclipse Capital' (Manufacturing Dive, Voxel Matters). It began as Formation 8's hardware fund (TechCrunch 2016); EDGAR shows Formation8 Partners Hardware Fund I, L.P. (CIK 1641394, Form D 2015-05-20) refiled as Eclipse Ventures Fund I, L.P. under the same CIK. EDGAR full-text search for Form Ds naming Lior Susan lists the flagship funds (Eclipse Fund II–VI, L.P.), Eclipse Early Growth Fund I–III, Eclipse Continuity Fund I, Eclipse Partners Fund I/IV/V/VI and deal SPVs Eclipse SPV I–XXXVII, L.P., all at Palo Alto, CA. Not Titan Eclipse Fund LP (Stamford, CT), not Hunters Moon Eclipse Fund LP/Ltd (Cayman), not Crawling Stone Capital (EDGAR hits for 'Eclipse Fund'), not the Eclipse Foundation (open-source IDE) or the Eclipse blockchain network, and not Parallax Worlds (separate cache file; the Parallax here is a turbine maker).

application_url is the About page, whose 'Submit a Business Plan' link is a mailto to the firm's admin address (not recorded); no web form found.

Partner bios: eclipse.capital/team/<slug> pages did not render bio text for fetching; partner focus_sectors are inferred from deals each partner wrote up on the Eclipse blog. No personal LinkedIn URLs are linked from the firm's site.

Parallax seed date: only disclosed on 2026-09-24 (stealth exit); close date not stated. Whether Eclipse joined the $75M Series A (Greylock, General Catalyst) is not stated. The post's wording leaves unclear whether Lux Capital, Founders Fund and Valor co-led or participated.
